sources: The $1.5B acquisition adds AI-driven customer data capabilities to Diginex's sustainability and compliance platform — transforming it from a point solution into an integrated end-to-end platform.
prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: pale cyan. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them. Every cutout is matte paper reflecting only the room light, with a plain blank face: coin rims, document faces, screens and vehicle sides carry no lettering, numerals or marks.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons, tape, rubber stamps, string and pins, stencilled arrows, paper bar charts, stacked sheets, grid paper, torn strips, hole-punched tags, paper clips, in cream, black, pale yellow or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture and print dots.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip: one line, no wider than a third of the frame width, with safe margins, the chip sitting clear of the subjects. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw. When the beat marks a hero number, that number alone may be printed larger, up to half the frame width.
8. Compositions vary in scale from beat to beat: some show one oversized subject filling the frame, some a small subject alone on open ground, some several elements arranged as a diagram.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: pale cyan.
Subjects: stacked paper sheets; paper clips.
Opens on the coin stack, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The previous chip flips away as the coin stack flattens into stacked paper sheets; paper clips slide on and bind the sheets into one block.
Ends holding on the bound block.
This composition is small-scale: a single subject sits alone on open ground.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "END-TO-END".

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "END-TO-END". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "It turns a point solution into an integrated platform.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a cinematic, modern editorial paper collage style video. The scene opens on <Picture 1>, featuring a purple paper ground with a cream paper chip reading "REVENUE SYNERGY" and a large torn-paper cutout of a "SYNERGY" stamp. Immediately, the camera remains as a Static Shot. Within the first second, the existing purple ground, the "REVENUE SYNERGY" chip, and the stamp cutout slide rapidly off-frame to the left with a slight overshoot, revealing a new, flat, unbroken pale cyan paper ground. Simultaneously, a new cream-colored paper chip lands firmly in the upper third of the frame; printed on it in an extra-bold black sans-serif typeface is the text "END-TO-END", which remains clean, legible, and stable. In the center of the lower two-thirds of the frame, a small-scale composition forms: a stack of black-and-white halftone photographic coins (carried over from the previous beat) rapidly flattens and transforms into a neat stack of blank, unmarked white paper sheets. These sheets feature rough white torn-paper edges and a matte texture. Immediately following the flattening, several small silver paper clips slide in from the edges of the frame with fast motion and a slight overshoot, binding the stacked sheets into one solid block. The entire scene is illuminated by a consistent light from the upper left, casting small, soft, realistic shadows beneath every paper layer. The final two seconds hold on this bound block of paper on the open cyan ground, with a subtle, rhythmic breathing loop of the elements to maintain dynamism. (S1), a narrator with a warm, clear, natural, and brisk English voice, says <d>[English] It turns a point solution into an integrated platform.</d> beginning on the first frame; the narrator is off-screen.

overall_soundscape: The audio is dominated by the crisp, tactile sounds of a paper studio. Distinct, sharp paper-slap sounds occur as the elements slide and land, accompanied by the metallic, clicking sound of paper clips sliding and snapping onto the sheets.
